Filmhounds Magazine editor-in-chief and Tomatometer critic Gavin Spoors praised the film’s third act as “stellar,” writing that it “pulls the rug out underneath you.” “Anchored by terrific performances (Zada is a star), this emotional thriller nails the themes of the cost of revolution and how we all need to play our part,” he wrote on X .

Matt Neglia, Next Best Picture editor-in-chief, wrote that the film “features some of the best casting of the year” in his review. “Many of the actors breathe new life into familiar characters, making them their own, while preserving the qualities that made them so compelling in the first place,” he continued. “Glenn Close, with her horror-inducing face, is a scene-stealer as is Jesse Plemons embodying the spirit of the late great Philip Seymour Hoffman. Joseph Zada is beyond impressive in a highly demanding role that pushes him to the limit physically and emotionally, perfectly capturing the essence of Haymitch with all the sympathy, charm and bitterness Woody Harrelson brought to the role. I’m continually blown away by how Francis Lawrence continues to find more layers in this familiar structure thematically and stylistically as the production and costume design continue to be dazzling highlights. If this is to be the end of his time working on these movies, it’s a good way to go out as this latest installment brings the franchise full circle with the character that’s always been the beating heart at its center.”

“The rebellion is sparking with SUNRISE ON THE REAPING,” wrote fellow Next Best Picture editor Lauren LaMagna. “Francis Lawrence continues to breathe new life into this world. The unique production design doesn’t let familiar beats get too dull. Joseph Zada is heartbreakingly radiant as Haymitch. A star is born role.”

“One of the biggest highlights? Joseph Zada,” wrote Collider’s Perri Nemiroff. “I had high hopes for him after watching We Were Liars, but he had my jaw on the floor time and time again during Sunrise on the Reaping. His ability to capture Haymitch’s warmth and charm and then weave that into the rage and heartbreak the Hunger Games sparks is superb. SO much of this movie is on his shoulders, and he soars tackling every ounce of it. This is only the beginning for Zada.”

He continued : “Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes bolstered my rewatches of the original films, and I have no doubt the same will be true of Sunrise on the Reaping. Sparking real change can take time and demand great sacrifice. This film franchise is better off for having added Haymitch’s.”

Static Media writer Nina Starner also championed Zada’s casting, saying that it “couldn’t be better.” “ The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is a worthy addition to the franchise,” she wrote . “It looks and feels terrifyingly real, and it bridges the gap perfectly between the original stories and Ballad. A from me.”

Based on Suzanne Collins’ 2025 novel “Sunrise on the Reaping,” the latest “Hunger Games” movie centers on a young Haymitch (Zada, taking over the role from Woody Harrelson) as he fights to survive while competing in the 50th Hunger Games. The cast also features Jesse Plemons as Plutarch, Ralph Fiennes as President Snow, Kieran Culkin as Caesar Flickerman, Maya Hawke as Wiress and Kelvin Harrison Jr. as Beetee. New characters in the film franchise are played by the likes of Mckenna Grace, Glenn Close and Whitney Peak, among others.

“Sunrise on the Reaping” takes place 24 years before the start of the first “Hunger Games” movie. Frances Lawrence, who has directed every “Hunger Games” movie except for the first installment (that was Gary Ross), returns to helm the latest prequel movie.

Much of the buzz surrounding “Sunrise on the Reaping” has been related to the franchise returns of Jennifer Lawrence , Josh Hutcherson and Harrelson as Katniss, Peeta and Haymitch. Book readers know that Suzanne Collins’ novel ends with a flash-forward epilogue featuring the trio, so it appears the film adaptation is following suit.

“It was unbelievable,” Lawrence said on the “Call Her Daddy” podcast about reprising Katniss. “It was so crazy. It was the same crew. It was the same AD, who I’ve worked with a million times because I love him. And with Josh [Hutcherson] and Woody [Harrelson] … it was so emotional. Josh and I didn’t walk to the bathroom without our arms around each other. It was so beautiful.”

“The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” is set to open in theaters Nov. 20 from Lionsgate. Check out first reactions to the movie below.

article_text:
Georgina Cates , the actress known for her roles in Clay Pigeons (1998) and several BBC projects, has died. She was 51.

On Saturday, BBC’s 2point4 Children creator Andrew Marshall announced Cates’ passing, years after her breakout role as Jenny Porter on the sitcom when she was 16. She had reportedly died in May, and a cause of death was not immediately made available.

Related Stories

2026 Deaths Photo Gallery: Hollywood & Media Obituaries

Michael Gray Dies: ‘Shazam!’ Star Was 75

“I’m very sad to report, I have just discovered, that lovely and talented Claire Woodgate aka Georgina Cates, our first Jenny in 2p4 died last May,” wrote Marshall on X . “I have no other details than than on IMDb. Sympathies to her family and children. If anyone has further details to share, please do.”

Marshall’s post comes after Cates and ex-husband Skeet Ulrich’s daughter Naiia announced her mother’s death in June.

“My beautiful, free-spirited mom lived a hard life and still found ways to make herself and others laugh and smile <3 now she can rest easy,” she wrote on Instagram . “I will always see you in black and white photos, Virginia slims, baggy clothes, no bras, big sunglasses, doodling while talking, pleasers, and flip flops and everything in between.”

I’m very sad to report, I have just discovered, that lovely and talented Claire Woodgate aka Georgina Cates, our 1st Jenny in 2p4 died last May. I have no other details than than on IMDb. Sympathies to her family and children. If anyone has further details to share, please do. — Andrew Marshall (@AndrewM2p4c) October 17, 2026

Naiia continued, “I love you, thank you for your creativity, curiosity and your bravery to always be true to yourself – no matter what.”

Born Claire Elaine Woodgate on April 4, 1975 in Colchester, Essex, England, Cates broke out in the first two seasons of 2point4 before appearing in such shows as The Ruth Rendell Mysteries and The Bill and Chris Cross . Her movies credits included An Exchange of Fire (1993), Au Pair (1994), An Awfully Big Adventure (1995), Frankie Starlight (1995), Big City Blues (1997) and A Soldier’s Sweetheart (1998).

Also in 1998, Cates earned acclaim for her performance as Amanda in the Ridley Scott-produced Clay Pigeons , also starring Vince Vaughn and Joaquin Phoenix.

In 2007, following a years-long hiatus from acting, Cates won the Best Actress in a Leading Role award for her performance in Sinner during the 41st Brooklyn Arts Council International Film & Video Festival.

Cates is survived by her children Naiia and Jakob, whom she shared with ex-husband Ulrich.

article_text:
Films and events

Debate

My Undesirable Friends: Part II – Exile

The second part of Julia Loktev’s epic documentary, detailing the persecution of journalists in Russia, follows her brave protagonists’ escape abroad following the country’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Julia Loktev

USA 2026. 370min (includes 15min interval)

Courtesy of Cinetic

Language Russian With English subtitles

Introduction

Part one of this extraordinary undertaking chronicled the work of young female journalists who faced growing repression by Vladimir Putin’s regime in the lead-up to the 2022 invasion of Ukraine. This new instalment proves even more troubling, finding the journalists scattered across different countries and grappling with their new lives, while still struggling to continue their reporting on Russia.

Sergio Fant

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Mariinka

Shot over ten years, this unflinching portrait of youth in Eastern Ukraine is a rare and powerful account of the passing of time during conflict.

The Whisper of Sunlight

Acclaimed documentarian Wong Siu-pong’s moving film creates an intimate space in which three young women with terminal conditions navigate experiences of illness, care and companionship.

Imperium

Master of archival film reconstruction, Sergei Loznitsa, reframes Soviet history once again via the revealing gaze of Italian cameramen who captured life there in the early 1970s.

article_text:
Source: Moonspun Films

‘I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning’

Clio Barnard’s I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning has won the best film prize in the Progressive Cinema competition at the Rome Film Fest, which wrapped today (October 24).

Barnard’s Birmingham-set drama centres on a group of childhood friends on the cusp of their 30 th birthdays who are forced to confront a life where their hopes and dreams haven’t materialised. It previously won the People’s Choice award in Cannes’ Directors’ Fortnight where it world premiered.

One of the film’s leads, Anthony Boyle, shared the best actor prize at Rome for his role in I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning along with Paolo Pierobon for Italian noir drama Brianza.

Rome’s Progressive Cinema competition gave its jury grand prize to prison drama The Life And Deaths Of Wilson Shedd by Tim Blake Nelson. Amanda Seyfried stars as an English teacher trapped in an abusive marriage, who takes a job at a maximum-security prison in Oklahoma and forms an intense connection with a charismatic inmate in her class.

The best screenplay prize went to Abia Castillo, Diego Rabasa and Diego Luna for migrant drama Ashes , directed by Luna.

The best director prize was awarded to Rafiki Fariala for Congo Boy , which also shared the festival’s audience award with Nepal-set documentary Mustang by Kasia Smutniak.

Victoria Luengo won best actress for her role in Spanish heist thriller Saints . The competition’s special jury prize went to the Al Mawla family for Yesterday the Eye Didn’t Sleep, which centres on a Palestinian family forced to flee because of a blood feud with another family from a different tribe in the Lebanese Bekaa Valley.

The Progressive Cinema competition jury was chaired by Polish filmmaker Jan Komasa, joined by actors Alice Braga and Saja Kilani and filmmakers Carlos Marques-Marcet and Alessio Rigo de Righi.

Meanwhile, Rome Film Fest’s best first feature prize went to Clementine Orange by Swedish filmmaker Lisa Forslund, which world premiered in the festival’s Freestyle section. The film focuses on a young woman who has fallen in love with a prisoner whose letters and photos have sparked fantasies of a dangerous, forbidden love.

A special mention was given to debut feature The River Train by Lorenzo Ferro and Lucas A. Vignale, which also played in the Freestyle section.

The first feature jury was chaired by the Italian filmmaker Ludovica Rampoldi, joined by French director Pauline Loquès and the Romanian filmmaker Corneliu Porumboiu.

The festival’s documentary prize was awarded to Into The Jaws Of The Ogre by Mahsa Karampour, while a special mention went to A Russian Winter by Patric Chiha. Both documentaries played in Rome’s Special Screenings section.

The documentary jury was chaired by Italian director Roberto Minervini, joined by Spanish producer Andrea Queralt and Argentine-British actor Jessica Sarah Rinland.

Rome’s Banca Ifis music award went to Nicola Piovani, while the Gillo Pontecorvo Award went to Emmanuel Marre for Notre Salut.

During the festival, Rome gave its industry lifetime achievement award to UK producer Tessa Ross, lifetime achievement awards to Javier Bardem and Julianne Moore, and its progressive lifetime achievement award to Anthony Ippolito.

The festival reported 82,238 tickets sold and 4,651 accreditations. It screened 194 films across 527 screenings.

article_text:
Dolly vinha enfrentando problemas de saúde desde o início do ano e já havia adiado seu retorno aos palcos

Um dos maiores ícones do entretenimento estadunidense, a cantora Dolly Parton morreu nesta terça-feira (25). Ela vinha enfrentando problemas de saúde desde o início do ano e já havia adiado seu retorno aos palcos.

O anúncio oficial foi feito pelo sobrinho de Dolly, Bryan Seaver, a pedido dela própria. Veja abaixo.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dolly Parton (@dollyparton)

Dolly Parton marcou época como um dos principais nomes da música country nos EUA, empilhando clássicos como “Jolene”, “I Will Always Love You”, “9 to 5” e “Islands In the Stream”, entre tantas outras. Sua figura tornou-se sinônimo de sucesso, influenciando artistas de todos os gêneros e mídias. Além de cantora e compositora, Dolly também foi produtora, dramaturga, filantropa, autora e fundadora de seu próprio parque temático, Dollywood, no estado do Tennessee.

Comprovando seu talento e impacto na indústria, Dolly conquistou 11 Grammys entre 54 indicações, além de integrar os Halls da Fama do Rock & Roll, da Música Country e dos Compositores. Além de seu sucesso no Grammy, ela conquistou também um Emmy, prêmio máximo da televisão dos EUA, dentre cinco indicações, e foi indicada duas vezes ao Oscar de Melhor Canção Original. Em 1981, ela concorreu com a canção “9 to 5”, do filme “Como Eliminar Seu Chefe”, que estrelou junto a Jane Fonda e Lily Tomlin. Já em 2006, Dolly foi indicada pela canção “Travelin’ Thru”, do filme “Transamérica”. Duas décadas depois, ela recebeu o Prêmio Humanitário Jean Hersholt da Academia em 2026.

Dolly Parton não deixa filhos, mas deixa um legado incomparável e duradouro.
